---
title: From Quarto
description: What is different from Quarto, and how to check a project before you move it.
order: 8
---

smalldocs builds the website part of Quarto. A project that uses only that part builds with either
tool. The two builds give the same pages, the same anchors and the same links.

Check a project first:

```bash
smalldocs check docs
```

The command builds the site into a temporary folder. Then it lists what smalldocs does not read:

- each option that smalldocs ignores
- each broken link
- each piece of Pandoc's Markdown that smalldocs does not read, with its file and its line

If the command finds anything, its exit code is 1.

## What works

smalldocs reads most of the options of Quarto for a website. [The configuration](config.qmd) lists
them, with the default of each. [Writing pages](markdown.qmd) shows the Markdown that smalldocs reads.
This Markdown includes callouts, tabsets, figures, table captions, footnotes, the margin, maths, diagrams
and shortcodes.

A site also gets listings, search, a light and a dark theme, comments and Google
Analytics, as in Quarto. A notebook shows its saved outputs, with the options of its cells. See
[Notebooks](notebooks.ipynb).

## What smalldocs does not do yet

smalldocs gives a warning for each of these options, or shows the Markdown as text:

| Quarto | smalldocs |
|---|---|
| Cross-references, such as `@fig-a`, `@tbl-a`, `@sec-a` and `@eq-a`, with numbers, and the `crossref` options | Not read. Write a link to the id, such as `[the table](#tbl-a)` |
| Figure divs, `::: {#fig-a}`, and subfigures | Not read. A picture alone in its paragraph is a figure |
| Labels on equations, `$$...$$ {#eq-a}` | Not read |
| A negative width in `layout`, for an empty space | Not read. The other widths work |
| Code annotations, `# <1>` | Not read |
| Example lists, `(@)`, and line blocks, `\|` | Not read |
| `lightbox`, `footnotes-hover`, `reader-mode`, `code-tools`, `highlight-style` | Not read |
| `website.announcement`, `body-header`, `body-footer`, `margin-header`, `margin-footer`, `cookie-consent` | Not read |
| `listing`: `image-placeholder`, `image-align`, `image-lazy-loading`, `field-types`, `field-links`, `field-required` | Not read |
| `search`: `copy-button`, `collapse-after`, `show-item-context`, `merge-navbar-crumbs` | Not read |
| `_brand.yml` | Not read. Use a [theme](themes.qmd), or the [options for fonts and colours](themes.qmd#fonts-and-colours-from-options) |
| Citations and a bibliography | Not read |

## What smalldocs will not do

| Quarto | smalldocs |
|---|---|
| PDF, Word, slides, books, manuscripts | Websites only. A `book` is built as a website |
| Runs `{python}`, `{r}` and `{ojs}` cells, with `jupyter`, `freeze`, `cache`, `engine` and `df-print` | Shows the code and runs nothing. A notebook shows its saved outputs. Each of these options gives a warning |
| Compiles `.scss` themes | Takes any Bootswatch theme, your CSS, and the CSS of a theme extension. See [Themes](themes.qmd) |
| `embed-resources` and `self-contained` | Not read. The pages load the stylesheets and the scripts from `site_libs` |
| Lua filters | Runs no Lua. The [linkify](config.qmd#linkify) of smalldocs does the work of `linkify.lua`, but links only names that look like code. See [Lua filters](config.qmd#lua-filters) |
| Graphviz `{dot}` blocks | Not read. Make an SVG with Graphviz, and use it as a picture |
| `listing.template`, `about` pages, Algolia search | Not read. A listing is a default, grid or table listing, and search reads `search.json` |
| Grid tables and raw LaTeX | `smalldocs check` reports them. Write a pipe table |

## Different defaults

Two defaults of smalldocs differ from Quarto. They stay, so that sites that exist do not change:

- The key `/` goes to the search box. Quarto also uses `f` and `s`. See [Search](config.qmd#search).
- A figure starts at the left of the column. Quarto puts it in the centre. See
  [Figures](markdown.qmd#figures).

## What is the same

- smalldocs reads `_quarto.yml`, and merges it with `_metadata.yml` and front matter in the same order
  as Quarto.
- smalldocs makes the ids of headings by the rules of Pandoc. So links and anchors that were written
  for Quarto keep working.
- A link to a `.qmd`, `.md` or `.ipynb` file becomes a link to the `.html` file. A link that starts with
  `/` starts at the root of the project.
- The HTML of the page has the same classes and ids as in Quarto, such as `#quarto-sidebar`, `#TOC`,
  `.callout-note`, `.panel-tabset` and `.quarto-grid-item`. So most CSS that was written for a Quarto
  site works.
- smalldocs runs `pre-render` and `post-render` with the same environment variables as Quarto.

## Move a project

1. Run `smalldocs check`, and fix what it lists.
2. Run `smalldocs preview`. Compare each page with the page that Quarto made.
3. In the recipe that builds the site, change `quarto render` to `smalldocs render`. Change
   `quarto publish gh-pages` to `smalldocs publish gh-pages`.
4. If a script of the project writes its API reference, use the `api` section of smalldocs instead.
   Remove the script from `pre-render`. See [The API reference](api.qmd).
5. When Quarto no longer builds the project, change `_quarto.yml` to `_smalldocs.yml`. See
   [A _quarto.yml](config.qmd#a-_quarto.yml).
